correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, two omitted vertices on each row must either both be singleton blocks or form an adjacent hook; this gives W_n independent half-decorations. The two inner decorations fall into three disjoint intersection classes, subdivided by hook status into exactly seven cases. The proof traces connected components in each case, counts each class with explicit binomial/adjacent-edge formulas, and independently counts free outer decorations. Coefficients sum to W_n^4, and full graph-gluing enumeration over n=3,4,5,6 agrees for all 205,602 pairs. Finite tests are not presented as a universal proof.

Primary literature arXiv:1512.02279 introduces rank classes, loop/path twisting and cell modules, while arXiv:1106.5277 treats diagram algebra and arXiv:1301.4518 the monoid presentation; none states these seven aggregate coefficients. value.rationale: Corank two is not arbitrary: it is the lowest Motzkin rank where a nontransversal hook is possible. The seven strata expose three competing intrinsic multiplication effects—floating singleton paths, closed loops that weight the twisted algebra, and an alternating double-hook strand that raises product rank relative to naive missing-set overlap. Their complete joint polynomial, rather than a single numerical constant, is a useful natural multiplication invariant for every n>=3; loop probability is exactly 4/((n-1)(n+2)^2).
